newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian GIA threatened France before bomb - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian GIA threatened France before bomb - paper.

text.p: Algeria's Armed Islamic Group (GIA) issued threats against France three months before the deadly bomb which exploded on a Paris train on Tuesday, a newspaper reported on Thursday.

"France fights Moslems, that's why we maintain the same attitude towards this country as our predecessors, the emirs of the GIA," Liberation quoted GIA leader Antar Zouabri as writing in the clandestine Al Jamaar newsletter on September 10.
The bomb at the Port Royal station on a suburban rail line killed a Canadian woman and a Frenchman and injured 88. Police said it bore the hallmarks of Islamic guerrillas.
Zouabri has replaced Djamel Zitouni, who had claimed responsibility for "attacks at the heart of France" in 1995.

Those bombings in Paris and Lyon, which killed eight people and injured more than 160 others, were launched because of France's support for the Algiers government, fighting a violent campaign by Islamic guerrillas, and the deaths of Algerian hijackers of an Air France airbus in December 1994.
Investigators had earlier said that Zouabri had "taken up in various statements the anti-French stance of his predecessor, Djamel Zitouni".
